name: Vidhana Soudha
description: Karnataka’s neo-Dravidian legislature building is a defining Bengaluru landmark, best viewed from the public approaches around Cubbon Park.
how_to_reach: Reach central Bengaluru by Metro, bus, taxi or auto-rickshaw; the nearest Metro stations are Cubbon Park and Dr. B. R. Ambedkar Vidhana Soudha.
practical_notes: The legislature is not a walk-in tourist monument. Observe security restrictions and use designated public viewpoints. Seasonal lighting and access arrangements vary.
entry_fee: Public exterior viewing; access restrictions apply

name: Mysuru Palace
description: The former royal palace of Mysuru combines Indo-Saracenic architecture, ceremonial halls and an important place in the city’s Dasara traditions.
how_to_reach: Located in central Mysuru, reachable by city bus, taxi or auto-rickshaw from Mysuru Junction and the airport.
practical_notes: Ticketing, illuminated-evening displays and holiday hours vary. Confirm current visitor rules with Karnataka Tourism before travel.

name: Badami Cave Temples
description: Rock-cut cave temples carved into red sandstone cliffs above Agastya Lake, representing early Chalukyan art and architecture.
how_to_reach: Badami is reached by road and rail from Hubballi, Bengaluru and Vijayapura; local vehicles connect the station and cave complex.
practical_notes: October to March is generally more comfortable. Monument timings and entry charges should be confirmed before visiting.

name: Hampi Group of Monuments
description: A UNESCO World Heritage landscape of Vijayanagara-era temples, markets, tanks and boulder-strewn hills around the Tungabhadra River.
how_to_reach: Hospet is the main rail and road gateway; continue by taxi, bus, bicycle or authorised local transport to Hampi.
practical_notes: Allow multiple days for the spread-out sites. Protected-monument ticketing, electric vehicle rules and heat conditions vary by season.

name: Gokarna and Om Beach
description: Gokarna combines a pilgrimage town with a series of Arabian Sea coves, including the distinctive crescent-shaped Om Beach.
how_to_reach: Reach Gokarna by Konkan Railway, coastal highway buses or taxi from Goa, Hubballi or Mangaluru.
practical_notes: Beach conditions change during the monsoon. Swim only where local safety guidance permits and respect temple customs in town.

name: Bandipur Tiger Reserve
description: A major dry-deciduous forest reserve in the Nilgiri landscape, known for regulated safari access and wildlife habitat shared with adjoining protected areas.
how_to_reach: The reserve is reached by road from Mysuru, Bengaluru and Ooty; use authorised forest department entry points.
practical_notes: Safari permits, zones, timings and seasonal closures are controlled by the forest department. Wildlife sightings are never guaranteed.
entry_fee: Forest safari and entry charges apply

name: Nandi Hills
description: A hilltop getaway north of Bengaluru known for cooler mornings, viewpoints and historic hill-station remains.
how_to_reach: Reach by road from Bengaluru or Chikkaballapura; pre-dawn trips require checking current gate and vehicle rules.
practical_notes: Weekend sunrise visits can be crowded. Confirm entry hours, parking rules and weather conditions before leaving Bengaluru.
entry_fee: Check current entry and parking charges

name: Mullayanagiri Peak
description: Karnataka’s highest peak rises above the coffee country around Chikkamagaluru, with mountain roads, walking routes and broad Western Ghats views.
how_to_reach: Travel by road from Chikkamagaluru town using a local taxi or suitable private vehicle.
practical_notes: Fog, rain and wind can make the route hazardous. Follow local access instructions and avoid off-trail hiking.
entry_fee: No standard entry fee; local parking charges may apply

name: Chitradurga Fort
description: A vast hill fort of layered stone walls, gateways, reservoirs and lookout points associated with the Nayakas of Chitradurga.
how_to_reach: Chitradurga is on the Bengaluru–Pune highway and rail corridor; local transport connects the town and fort.
practical_notes: The fort has steep, uneven terrain. Carry water, wear shoes with grip and confirm ASI opening hours.

name: St. Mary’s Islands
description: A small offshore island group known for distinctive columnar basalt formations and reached by seasonal boat services from the Udupi coast.
how_to_reach: Take an authorised boat from Malpe; Udupi is connected by rail and road to Mangaluru and Bengaluru.
practical_notes: Boat operations depend on sea conditions and may pause in monsoon. Confirm schedules, life-jacket rules and last-return timings.
entry_fee: Boat and local entry charges apply

name: Murudeshwar Temple and Beach
description: A coastal pilgrimage town centred on the Murudeshwar Shiva temple complex, a large statue and a beach-facing setting.
how_to_reach: Murudeshwar has a railway station on the Konkan line and is accessible by coastal road from Mangaluru, Udupi and Goa.
practical_notes: Temple and tower access rules can change. Dress modestly for worship areas and follow local sea-safety instructions.
entry_fee: Temple entry is generally free; tower access may be charged

name: Jog Falls
description: The Sharavathi River drops through a dramatic gorge at Jog Falls, a seasonal spectacle whose flow and viewpoints vary substantially through the year.
how_to_reach: Reach by road from Shivamogga, Sagara or Honnemardu; the nearest rail and bus links are at Sagara.
practical_notes: Monsoon brings the strongest flow but also wet, slippery conditions. Use marked viewpoints and check local access restrictions.

name: Chennakeshava Temple, Belur
description: A finely detailed Hoysala temple at Belur, recognised with nearby Hoysala monuments as part of the UNESCO World Heritage Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas.
how_to_reach: Belur is reached by road from Hassan, Chikkamagaluru and Mysuru; taxis and buses are available from Hassan.
practical_notes: This is an active temple as well as a protected heritage site. Dress respectfully and confirm photography and ticket rules on arrival.
entry_fee: Check current monument and camera charges

name: Gol Gumbaz
description: The monumental mausoleum of Mohammed Adil Shah is known for its enormous dome and whispering gallery, a landmark of Deccan architecture.
how_to_reach: Vijayapura is served by rail and road from Hubballi, Solapur, Bengaluru and Hyderabad; use local transport from the city centre.
practical_notes: Confirm ASI hours and ticketing. The gallery is reached by steps and can be crowded in peak season.

name: Bidar Fort
description: A later-medieval Deccan fort complex with broad ramparts, palace remains and waterworks reflecting Bidar’s Bahmani and Barid Shahi history.
how_to_reach: Bidar is reached by rail and road from Hyderabad, Kalaburagi and Bengaluru; the fort is accessible from town by local transport.
practical_notes: Explore only marked areas and confirm monument opening hours before visiting.

name: Dandeli and Kali River
description: Dandeli is a Western Ghats base for forest stays, river-based adventure and regulated access to the Kali landscape.
how_to_reach: Reach Dandeli by road from Hubballi, Goa or Karwar; the nearest railhead is Alnavar, with onward road transport.
practical_notes: Rafting and water activities depend on releases, weather and licensed operators. Verify safety standards, age limits and current availability.

name: Coorg Coffee Country
description: The Kodagu highlands around Madikeri are known for coffee estates, forested roads, waterfalls and a distinct regional culture.
how_to_reach: Madikeri is reached by road from Bengaluru, Mysuru and Mangaluru. The nearest major rail link is Mysuru.
practical_notes: Estate visits require permission. Monsoon is scenic but can bring landslides and restricted waterfall access; check local advisories.

name: Nagarhole National Park
description: Nagarhole is a major tiger reserve in the Nilgiri Biosphere landscape, visited through regulated safari zones and forest department gates.
how_to_reach: Access is by road from Mysuru, Madikeri or Hunsur; use authorised safari booking channels and designated gates.
practical_notes: Safaris are regulated and sightings cannot be promised. Book through authorised channels and follow forest department instructions.
entry_fee: Forest safari and entry charges apply

name: Sringeri Sharada Peetham
description: A major Advaita monastic centre on the Tunga River, associated with Adi Shankaracharya and centred on the Sharadamba temple.
how_to_reach: Sringeri is reached by road from Chikkamagaluru, Udupi and Shivamogga; local buses and taxis serve the town.
practical_notes: It is an active religious institution. Dress modestly, respect ritual spaces and confirm festival-period access locally.

name: Dharmasthala Manjunatha Temple
description: Dharmasthala is a major pilgrimage town known for the Manjunatha temple, charitable traditions and its multi-faith heritage.
how_to_reach: Reach by road from Mangaluru, Udupi or Bengaluru. Local bus and taxi services connect the temple area.
practical_notes: Follow temple dress and queue rules. Festival dates and special darshan arrangements should be confirmed with official temple channels.
entry_fee: Free general entry; special services vary

name: Pattadakal Group of Monuments
description: A UNESCO World Heritage ensemble of early Chalukyan temples where northern and southern Indian architectural traditions meet along the Malaprabha valley.
how_to_reach: Pattadakal is reached by road from Badami and Bagalkote; Hubballi is a larger transport gateway.
practical_notes: Visit in cooler hours and confirm ASI ticketing. Combine with Badami and Aihole only with enough daylight for travel.
